clinicalPearls: Consider EoE in young adults (often male) presenting with recurrent solid-food dysphagia or food bolus impaction, especially with a personal or family history of atopy, asthma, or allergic rhinitis.
In children, presentation is often less specific - feeding difficulty, vomiting, abdominal pain, or failure to thrive rather than classic dysphagia.

Endoscopy may show characteristic esophageal rings ('trachealization'), linear furrows, whitish exudates/plaques, and mucosal fragility ('crepe-paper' esophagus), but can appear normal in a subset of patients.
Diagnosis requires both compatible clinical symptoms and esophageal biopsies showing eosinophil-predominant inflammation, after excluding other causes of esophageal eosinophilia.

Proton pump inhibitor-responsive esophageal eosinophilia exists on the same clinical spectrum and no longer excludes an EoE diagnosis; PPIs are considered a treatment option rather than purely a diagnostic exclusion test.
Take multiple biopsies (typically several from proximal and distal esophagus) since eosinophilic infiltration can be patchy.
Dietary elimination approaches (empiric or allergy-testing-directed) and topical swallowed corticosteroids are mainstay therapies alongside consideration of PPIs.
Esophageal dilation may be needed for fibrostenotic disease but carries a higher perforation risk than in other esophageal strictures due to mucosal fragility.
harrison.pathophysiology: Eosinophilic oesophagitis is a chronic, immune/antigen-mediated condition in which food and aeroallergens drive a Th2-skewed inflammatory response leading to dense eosinophilic infiltration of the esophageal mucosa. Persistent inflammation promotes epithelial barrier dysfunction and, over time, subepithelial fibrosis and smooth muscle remodeling, producing the strictures, rings, and narrow-caliber esophagus seen in longstanding disease. It is closely linked to atopic disease and shares overlapping pathways with asthma, allergic rhinitis, and atopic dermatitis.
additionalDifferentials: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) with secondary esophageal eosinophilia
Achalasia and other esophageal motility disorders
Esophageal webs, Schatzki ring, or peptic stricture from other causes
additionalInvestigations: Upper endoscopy with multiple esophageal biopsies (proximal and distal) - required to confirm eosinophil-predominant inflammation and exclude mimics
Histology quantifying peak eosinophil count per high-power field - supports diagnostic threshold for EoE
Trial of acid suppression before/around diagnostic biopsy - helps distinguish reflux-related eosinophilia from primary EoE
Barium esophagram - useful to characterize strictures, rings, or narrow-caliber esophagus, particularly pre-dilation
Allergy evaluation (skin prick/patch or specific IgE testing) - may help guide elimination diet strategy though imperfect at predicting food triggers
Esophageal functional/impedance-pH testing - considered when reflux contribution is uncertain
Peripheral eosinophil count and total IgE - sometimes elevated but neither sensitive nor specific
Repeat endoscopy with biopsy after treatment - used to assess histologic response to dietary or pharmacologic therapy
redFlags: Acute food bolus impaction causing complete dysphagia - requires urgent endoscopic evaluation and possible removal
Suspected esophageal perforation, especially after dilation given increased mucosal fragility
Progressive weight loss or failure to thrive in pediatric patients
Signs of a tight fibrostenotic stricture on imaging/endoscopy before attempting dilation
Unexplained esophageal eosinophilia not responding to standard measures - reconsider alternative diagnoses (hypereosinophilic syndrome, Crohn disease)
pitfalls: Assuming a normal-appearing esophagus on endoscopy excludes EoE - mucosal appearance can be unremarkable despite significant histologic eosinophilia.
Relying on a single biopsy site, missing patchy involvement and underestimating eosinophil counts.
Treating all esophageal eosinophilia as pure GERD without considering the overlapping PPI-responsive EoE spectrum.
Performing aggressive dilation without recognizing the higher perforation risk from mucosal fragility and lack of prior gentle approach.
harrison.prognosis: EoE is a chronic, relapsing condition requiring long-term management; without maintenance therapy, symptoms and inflammation typically recur. Untreated or undertreated disease can progress to fibrostenotic remodeling with strictures and recurrent food impactions, but sustained dietary or pharmacologic control can maintain remission and reduce complications.
references: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e - Chapter on Diseases of the Esophagus / Eosinophilic Esophagitis
